title: dangling_reference analyzer — references to deleted first-party modules
intent: The inverse of dead_code. Dead-code asks 'does X have consumers?' (run before deleting X); this asks 'do X's consumers still have X?' (run after). MAINT-DEFER-009 deleted app/retopo/ as unused while examples/retopo/run.sh still ran `python -m app.retopo.run` and a CI job invoked it — callee deleted, callers left, structurally unfixable. This detector is the after-deletion half nobody ran.

scope.out_of_scope_notes: New analyzer only. Does NOT fix the real dangling reference the detector found in this repo (runner.py:24 `from code_audit.analyzers.base import Analyzer` under TYPE_CHECKING — analyzers/base.py does not exist; Analyzer lives in analyzers/__init__.py). That is a separate, unrelated fix, deliberately not bundled. The debt-ratchet baseline (baselines/main.json) is UNCHANGED: the debt snapshot tracks structural debt (god-functions, long parameter lists), not analyzer findings, and the analyzer was written to add zero new structural debt (fingerprint set identical to baseline). Symbol-level resolution deferred. Detectors B and C from the same handoff are separate PRs, not built here.

what_changed: New DanglingReferenceAnalyzer (id dangling_reference, version 1.0.0, rule DANGLING_REF_001): flags references to first-party modules absent from the tree.

Portable first-party discriminator: fire only when a reference's TOP-LEVEL package resolves in the tree but its FULL dotted path does not — naturally excludes missing third-party imports (their top-level resolves nowhere).

Module-granularity resolution across Python (import / from-import, AST) and unambiguous config contexts (python -m, inline import/from, TOML/cfg entry-points) in .sh/.yml/.yaml/.toml/.cfg/.ini/Makefile. Walks root directly (keeps .github, where CI-invoked deleted-module calls hide); ignores the Python-only `files` param so it is self-contained.
Every failure mode is a Finding, never a raised exception: any internal error becomes a LOW DANGLING_REF_ERROR finding; unparseable referencing files are skipped.

AnalyzerType.DANGLING_REFERENCE added; registered in api._DEFAULT_ANALYZERS; confidence_golden/confidence_policy/logic manifests refreshed for the new enum member (no version-anchor bump — no confidence-scoring change; order_dependence/hollow_guarantee precedent).

16 tests including the born-from-the-bug MAINT-DEFER-009 acceptance fixture. On self-scan the detector found one real dangling reference (runner.py:24 -> code_audit.analyzers.base); that fix is out of scope and deliberately not bundled. baselines/main.json is unchanged — the analyzer adds zero structural debt (debt-snapshot fingerprint set verified identical).
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: dead_code is explicitly single-file with cross-file analysis deferred; this is that cross-file sibling and the inverse question (do consumers still have the callee?). Distinct from the requirements/deployment analyzer, which owns missing third-party imports — this fires only on first-party paths.

commands_run: py -3.11 -m pytest tests/ -k "logic_manifest or golden or confidence_policy or signal_logic or registry_contract or public_rules or version_bump" -q
test_results: manifest/registry/version-bump contract tests: all passed after refresh.
Self-scan surfaced exactly one real dangling reference (runner.py:24 -> code_audit.analyzers.base); fix deferred, baseline unchanged (zero structural debt added).
verification.notes: Read-only detection; walks the real tree, no synthetic injection. Detector A of three; built alone and held for triage before B and C replicate the pattern.
